topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Mutation, clonal evolution and cancer susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arising in susceptible cells can support clonal evolution towards cancer in a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental contributions to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk and how confidently that contribution can be inferred.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive carcinogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example.

topics.label: Mechanisms of environmentally induced DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens damage DNA and generate mutations, often through the body's own metabolic processes.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutational initiation from the promotion of tumour growth by conditions that favour proliferation.

topics.label: Biological context and carcinogen susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain and consolidate how carcinogenic effects depend on the biological context in which exposure occurs.

topics.label: Assessing carcinogenicity and identifying causal exposures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the tools used to connect exposures with cancer and the limitations of the evidence those tools produce.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and framing exposure decisions as balances between risks and benefits.
